# Triangle-Multiset Lamina Mass Moments

## Purpose and Scope

This note describes the numerical kernel introduced for Tools #5503. Given
triangles already expressed in one orthonormal metre frame and one positive
total mass, it computes the center of mass and inertia tensor of a zero-thickness
lamina whose surface-mass density is proportional to unsigned triangle area.
The source is a triangle **multiset**: repeated faces count repeatedly. The
kernel is included in the manual for transparent review but is not yet a
registered or approved calculation. It does not load or admit a geometry asset,
establish frame authority, infer tissue ownership, model volume or thickness,
or qualify a native humanoid/body model.

## Design by Contract

### Preconditions

`vertices` must convert to a finite `float64` array of shape `(N, 3)`.
`faces` is an integer array of shape `(T, 3)` whose indices lie in `[0, N)`.
`mass` is a positive, finite, non-boolean scalar in kilograms. All vertex
coordinates are metres in one caller-declared orthonormal coordinate frame.
At least one input triangle must have positive representable area; each
nonzero area and its normalized fraction must be representable as a positive
`float64`, and total area must remain finite.

### Postconditions

The result reports the area-weighted center in metres and the center-of-mass
inertia tensor in kg m² for the declared lamina. It also reports total
unsigned area, zero-area face count, exact coincident positive-area face count,
and indexed boundary/nonmanifold edge counts. The duplicate diagnostic counts
each repeated coordinate face beyond its first occurrence. The compatible `InertiaResult`
uses `volume=0`, `was_watertight=False`, and the distinct
`triangle_multiset_lamina_mass` mode so it cannot imply a closed solid.

### Invariants

Reordering faces, translating the complete geometry, or applying a proper
rigid rotation preserves mass and scalar invariants; translation changes the
center by the same translation and does not change central inertia. Scaling
coordinates by a positive factor scales area by its square, preserves the
area fractions, and scales inertia by the square when total mass is held fixed.
Subdivision that preserves the geometric surface and area measure preserves
the moments within numerical tolerance. A repeated positive-area face retains
its multiplicity in both mass allocation and the diagnostic count.

## Coordinates, Frames, and Time

### Coordinate Frames

The function accepts coordinates in the caller's existing frame and performs
no frame transform. All vertices must use the same origin, axes, handedness,
and scale. No source-frame identifier is present in this numerical API; a
consumer that needs provenance or a native body frame must bind that separately
before calling it.

### Axis and Handedness

The covariance and inertia formulas use Euclidean three-dimensional vectors.
They are invariant to proper orthogonal basis rotation when both inputs and
outputs are transformed consistently. Triangle winding does not select a
normal or sign: area is unsigned and the represented surface has no orientation
semantics.

### Time Convention

This is a static geometry calculation and has no time, interpolation, or
integration policy. It cannot be used to infer a time-varying body shape.

## Units and Dimensions

### Symbol and Unit Table

| Symbol or field | Meaning | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $\mathbf{x}$, triangle vertices | Position in the common input frame | m |
| $A_i$, $A$ | Triangle area and total multiset area | m² |
| $w_i$ | Triangle area fraction | 1 |
| $m$ | Caller-specified total lamina mass | kg |
| $\mathbf{c}$ | Area-weighted center of mass | m |
| $\mathbf{C}$ | Mass-normalized central covariance | m² |
| $\mathbf{I}$ | Central inertia tensor | kg m² |

### Dimensional Checks

Area fractions are dimensionless. Nonzero areas and normalized face fractions
that underflow to zero in `float64` are rejected, not assigned zero mass or
reported as degenerate. No geometric area epsilon is used. The covariance has
units m² because it is an
area-weighted second central moment divided by total area. Multiplication by
mass yields kg m². The zero-thickness convention sets reported volume to 0 m³;
it is not an estimated enclosed volume.

## Derivation and Assumptions

### Assumptions

Each triangle carries uniform surface density, with one shared areal density
$\sigma=m/A$ over the entire input multiset. Mass is apportioned by unsigned
area. Triangles may be disconnected, overlap, coincide, or have inconsistent
winding; overlap is not removed. Degenerate zero-area triangles contribute no
mass and are reported separately. The derivation assumes ordinary Euclidean
coordinates and no thickness or volumetric contribution.

### Derivation

For triangle vertices $\mathbf{v}_{i1},\mathbf{v}_{i2},\mathbf{v}_{i3}$,

$$
A_i=\frac{1}{2}\left\|
(\mathbf{v}_{i2}-\mathbf{v}_{i1})\times
(\mathbf{v}_{i3}-\mathbf{v}_{i1})\right\|,\qquad
A=\sum_i A_i,\qquad w_i=\frac{A_i}{A}.
$$

The triangle centroid is $\mathbf{c}_i=(\mathbf{v}_{i1}+\mathbf{v}_{i2}+
\mathbf{v}_{i3})/3$, and the lamina center is
$\mathbf{c}=\sum_i w_i\mathbf{c}_i$. Uniform barycentric coordinates on one
triangle have covariance

$$
\mathbf{C}_i=\frac{1}{12}\sum_{k=1}^{3}
(\mathbf{v}_{ik}-\mathbf{c}_i)(\mathbf{v}_{ik}-\mathbf{c}_i)^T.
$$

Applying the law of total covariance over triangle identity and within-triangle
position gives

[]{#triangle-lamina-covariance}

$$
\mathbf{C}=\sum_i w_i\left[\mathbf{C}_i+
(\mathbf{c}_i-\mathbf{c})(\mathbf{c}_i-\mathbf{c})^T\right].
$$

For a mass distribution with central covariance $\mathbf{C}$,

[]{#triangle-lamina-inertia}

$$
\mathbf{I}=m\left[\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{C})\mathbf{1}_3-\mathbf{C}\right].
$$

This formula returns the standard inertia tensor, including signed
off-diagonal tensor components. `InertiaResult.as_urdf_dict()` exports those
same symmetric tensor entries as URDF `ixy`, `ixz`, and `iyz` coefficients.
The exporter does not negate them: an actual MuJoCo URDF loadback test checks
the reconstructed native tensor and kinetic energy for an asymmetric inertia.
This verifies that particular exporter/consumer path, not every URDF parser or
native engine.

## Algorithm

### Inputs

The public function `compute_triangle_lamina(vertices, faces, mass)` consumes
only the arrays and scalar above. It does not consume a path, mesh object,
transform, frame label, density, thickness, or native model.

### Procedure

1. Validate the mass and array shapes, finiteness, face dtype, and index bounds.
2. Gather indexed triangles and compute unsigned area weights.
3. Reject nonpositive or nonfinite total area; omit only exactly zero-area
   triangles from moment/topology accumulation.
4. Choose the first vertex of a maximum-area face as a local origin, then
   compute weighted center and central covariance in that translated frame.
5. Convert covariance to inertia and reject nonfinite center or tensor values.
6. Count exact duplicate positive-area coordinate triangles independent of
   winding, and count edge degree using source vertex indices.
7. Return a distinct lamina mode and explicit diagnostics without repairing or
   modifying source arrays.

The numerical arrays are vectorized over faces. Working memory is linear in
the number of input faces; uniqueness diagnostics sort/compare face and edge
records and are not a streaming algorithm.

### Outputs

`TriangleLaminaResult` contains an `InertiaResult`, total area, zero-area face
count, duplicate positive-area coordinate-face count, indexed boundary-edge
count, and indexed nonmanifold-edge count. The embedded legacy result object
remains mutable for compatibility. Counts are diagnostics, not mesh validation.

## Implementation Symbols

### Public Symbols

`compute_triangle_lamina` and `TriangleLaminaResult` are defined in
`src/shared/python/humanoid_character_builder/mesh/triangle_lamina.py`.
`InertiaMode.TRIANGLE_MULTISET_LAMINA_MASS` and the compatible
`InertiaResult` representation are defined in
`src/shared/python/humanoid_character_builder/mesh/inertia_calculator.py`.
This note does not assert that the module is a stable published consumer API.

### Source Mapping

The method maps to `_area_weights`, `_centered_moments`, and
`compute_triangle_lamina` in `triangle_lamina.py`; mode identity is mapped in
`inertia_calculator.py`. Analytic and metamorphic checks are in
`src/shared/python/humanoid_character_builder/tests/test_triangle_lamina.py`.
This kernel is separate from `MeshInertiaCalculator`, which derives solid
properties from volume-mesh processing and watertightness policy.

## Error and Failure Semantics

### Error Conditions

Wrong scalar kind or noninteger face indices raise `TypeError`. Invalid scalar
range, malformed/nonfinite vertices, face shape or bounds, no positive finite
total area, and nonfinite output moments raise `ValueError`. The function does
not repair malformed topology or substitute default mass/geometry.

### Recovery and Cancellation

The caller must correct source inputs and resubmit. There is no partial result,
fallback solid calculation, or cancellation callback. Large inputs are bounded
only by caller-provided memory and face count; this API provides no resource
budget or streaming cancellation guarantee.

## Uncertainty and Sensitivity

### Uncertainty Sources

This kernel propagates no uncertainty distribution. Its values depend on
caller-selected coordinates, mesh sampling, face multiplicity, declared mass,
and the unverified assumption of uniform area density. It does not determine
whether those assumptions are appropriate for an object or body segment.

### Sensitivity

Area and second moments are sensitive to coordinate perturbations and changes
in tessellation or face multiplicity. Very small representable positive areas
remain in the calculation; no tolerance silently removes them. Nonzero areas
or fractions not representable as positive `float64` are rejected. Summation
and floating-point rounding still affect results. The local-origin accumulation
reduces avoidable cancellation for translated geometry but does not provide an
error bound for every scale or conditioning regime.

## Verification and Validation

### Test Evidence

`test_triangle_analytic_mass_com_and_off_diagonal` checks the exact triangular
lamina result. Other tests check a rectangular plate and subdivision, an
analytic cube shell, rigid transforms/scaling/input immutability, duplicate
and degenerate faces, remote negligible-area faces, small representable and
unrepresentable areas, complex-coordinate rejection, and invalid input classes.
These are independent synthetic analytic or metamorphic tests; they are not
validation against a measured object or biomechanical segment.

### Acceptance Criteria

Numerical kernel acceptance requires finite typed inputs, correct analytic
moments, expected rigid-transform and subdivision invariants, explicit
degeneracy diagnostics, and fail-closed invalid-input behavior. Those criteria
do not establish source asset provenance, unit/frame correctness of a producer,
partial-overlap handling, biological mass distribution, or native-model
admission. The calculation freshness generator currently executes only the
D-plane pathway; this note therefore remains outside the registered calculation
set and cannot be represented as freshness-verified or exemplar-verified.

## Limits and Applicability

### Validity Range

The equations apply to a finite positive-area triangle multiset in one
orthonormal Euclidean metre frame with a positive finite caller-owned total
mass. Degenerate faces may be present but contribute no area or mass. No
evidence here establishes useful geometric scales beyond representable,
finite floating-point inputs.

### Known Limitations

Coincident triangles retain multiplicity; partial overlap is neither detected
nor corrected. Duplicate detection is exact-coordinate and ignores winding,
whereas edge topology uses vertex indices. Indexed boundary/nonmanifold counts
do not prove surface closure, manifoldness, or self-intersection absence. No
volume, thickness, density field, material, anatomy, frame transform, native
asset loader, downstream consumer or physical acceptance is included. The
registered calculation, freshness workflow, source asset producer and any
engineering-use approval remain blocked.

## Worked Examples

### Example Inputs

Use vertices $(0,0,0)$, $(3,0,0)$, and $(0,6,0)$ metres, one face with indices
$(0,1,2)$, and total mass $2$ kg. The triangle area is $9$ m² and the face
receives all of the declared mass.

### Example Results

The centroid is $(1,2,0)$ m. Integrating the uniform triangular area gives
$\mathbf{C}=\begin{bmatrix}1/2&-1/2&0\\-1/2&2&0\\0&0&0\end{bmatrix}$ m².
The returned inertia matrix is
$\mathbf{I}=\begin{bmatrix}4&1&0\\1&1&0\\0&0&5\end{bmatrix}$ kg m², with
all three indexed edges counted as boundary edges. The example verifies the
kernel's declared lamina equations; it is not an asset-backed exemplar or
evidence about a physical segment.
